clue.text: Black and white clothing starts to chafe kids in the team

indicators.note: one piece clothing another wraps around it, so the colour word goes outside

parts.note: pied means patched in black and white, like a magpie

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words give their opening letters

explanation.surface: A parent worries that a black-and-white strip rubs the children who have made the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who has been selected for a side has been picked, so 'in the team' describes the same state.

clue.text: Ubiquitous packaging company bottles wine

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: PLC is a public limited company
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A firm that puts wine into bottles is everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is the material found wrapping nearly every product on the shelves.

clue.text: Holiday flat swapped for the house?

definitions.meaning: in theatre a flat is a painted backdrop and the house is the audience, so new scenery is put up for them

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers trade their flat for a house by way of a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' and 'house' look like homes; in a theatre they are a painted backdrop and the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday gives a fresh setting, a change of scenery; on stage a scene change does it literally.

clue.text: Query after knives stuck in butter churned on truck

indicators.note: churning stirs butter about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ute is an Australian pickup truck, short for utility vehicle

explanation.surface: Something about churning butter while carving knives are left in it on a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned' turns BUTTER into ETTUBR. The words are Caesar's question to Brutus as he was stabbed, in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: "Et tu, Brute?" is Julius Caesar's dying question on seeing his friend Brutus among the stabbing assassins.

clue.text: Fine lines that chin gets after shaving unevenly

indicators.note: the phrase is trimmed by one letter at the front and three at the back, so the answer sits inside the words

explanation.surface: A man's jaw after a careless shave is left with a pattern of small marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after shaving unevenly' cuts T from the front of 'that chin gets' and ETS from the end, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In drawing and engraving, shading made from closely spaced parallel strokes is called hatching.

clue.text: Turn blade on steam-boat having lost pressure

indicators.note: something that has lost a part has it taken away

parts.note: a paddle steamer is driven by paddles, the blades of its wheel
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Instructions to rotate a paddle on a steamer that has lost steam pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to go bad, as an egg does; to turn is to go off, like milk.

clue.text: Make a soldier inspect lines

parts.note: to con is to study or scan closely
an actor's lines are written in the script

explanation.surface: An officer is told to look over the ranks to create a new recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To conscript is to enlist someone compulsorily into the armed forces, turning them into a soldier.

clue.text: Musician that's smart until ten is getting changed

indicators.note: letters being changed are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer stays in smart dress until ten, then changes into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting changed' rearranges the letters of 'smart until ten is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist is a player of a musical instrument, as opposed to a singer.

clue.text: D'Artagnan's home with a couple of rabbits

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chatter, and to gas is to chatter too
a couple asks for a second rabbit: a cony is the animal, an old word for rabbit

explanation.surface: The musketeer's homeland, pictured with a pair of rabbits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of rabbits' gives two: the verb rabbit (chatter, GAS) and the animal (CONY).
explanation.definitionFit: D'Artagnan, the hero of The Three Musketeers, came from Gascony in south-west France.

clue.text: Independently, Scottish poll indicates foreign laws widely hated

parts.note: to stand apart is to stand independently, on one's own
poll is an old word for head, and heid is the Scots form of head

explanation.surface: Reads like news that a Scottish independence vote points to unpopular laws from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish poll' looks like a referendum, but poll means head, in its Scots spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial segregation laws, condemned around the world.

clue.text: Maybe an ass covered in spangles gets cheeks pinched

indicators.note: cheeks are the two sides of a face, so both outer letters are taken off

parts.note: spangles are sequins, so a spangled garment is sequined

explanation.surface: A donkey in a glittery costume has its face pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: SEQUINED loses its outer letters S and D.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass belongs to the horse family, so it is an example of an equine animal.

clue.text: Sent abroad, son settles in the sticks?

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so the letters of the word are spread about

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone is posted overseas while their son makes a home out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sticks' looks like the countryside; here it is the twigs birds build homes from, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle into homes woven from twigs; to nest is to settle down, so nests means settles.

clue.text: Land, intending immediate departure?

definitions.meaning: food '...' is a takeaway, about to leave at once; read whole, '...' is about to depart

explanation.surface: A traveller's land, with the sense of someone poised to leave straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a West African nation, and 'to go' describes something set to leave, as in a takeaway order.

clue.text: Sailor selling freight caught on board A1 Greek ship

indicators.note: something on board a ship is inside it, so a letter goes into the ship's words

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, super
the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A seaman dealing in goods is arrested aboard a splendid Greek vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercargo is the officer on a merchant ship responsible for the cargo and its sale.

clue.text: Front or back half of train, Carol's deciding

indicators.note: either half of the train word is the same, so keeping one half gives the piece needed

parts.note: choo-choo is a child's word for a train
to carol is to sing, with 's as 'is' joining

explanation.surface: A girl called Carol picks which end of the train to sit in.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOO-CHOO is a child's word for a train; either half gives CHOO. 'Carol' looks like a name but is the verb sing.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose is to decide between options, so choosing is a synonym of deciding.

clue.text: One takes longer running cool wash with extra cold

indicators.note: a running wash cycle tumbles things about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A laundry cycle on a cool wash with an added cold rinse takes ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is a person who is slow and lags behind, taking longer than others.

clue.text: Policemen are within their rights to stun

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers
may expresses permission, being allowed to do something

explanation.surface: Officers say they are entitled to use a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay as a verb means to shock or appal someone, much as stun does.

clue.text: The sixth sense is related to wine

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
nous is common sense, gumption

explanation.surface: Looks like a claim that a sixth sense is linked to drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sixth sense' looks like intuition, but it splits into a Roman numeral and a word for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinous is an adjective meaning of or relating to wine, from Latin vinum.

clue.text: Practice docked damn cat

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to cuss is to swear, to damn
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone cursing a cat whose tail has been cut, with practice as the opening word.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is an established practice or habit, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Leave bank having emptied 'savings account' and duck into greasy spoon

indicators.note: putting pieces into another places them inside it

parts.note: a caff is a cheap British cafe, nicknamed a greasy spoon

indicators.note: an emptied phrase keeps only its outermost letters

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Someone clears out their savings and ducks into a cheap cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' keeps only the first and last letters of the whole phrase 'savings account'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat casts off when it unties its moorings and leaves the bank.

clue.text: Stone church used to store brown chicken feed

indicators.note: a container used to store something holds it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit
CE is the Church of England
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A stone church building doubles as a granary for poultry food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken feed is an idiom for a trivial sum of money, which is what a pittance is.

clue.text: Lord made poorly, died leaving his estate

indicators.note: poorly made suggests a botched arrangement of the letters
leaving signals that a letter departs from the jumble

explanation.surface: A lord falls ill and dies, leaving behind his landed property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' scrambles LORDMADE and 'leaving' takes out one D.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank and territory of an earl, the 'his' referring back to the Lord.

clue.text: Paper bound to note its owner's views

definitions.text: Paper bound to note its owner's views

parts.words: Paper bound to note its owner's views
parts.note: reads like paper obliged to record opinions; really bound pages for drawing the scenery an artist sees

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' seems to mean obliged and 'views' opinions; the pages are bound together and the views are scenes drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's pad of bound drawing paper holds sketches of the scenes its owner has looked at.

clue.text: See 3
Just a little short of quality

definitions.meaning: ... also means moderate, adequate but not excellent

explanation.surface: Something deemed just, yet falling slightly below a high standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair has both senses: equitable, and middling, as in a fair performance that is not quite good.

clue.text: Good vibrations pet sounds

explanation.surface: Two Beach Boys titles, Good Vibrations and Pet Sounds, put side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's purr is a low vibrating sound of contentment, the noise a pet makes.

clue.text: Nothing an American makes works

parts.note: O is the digit zero, nothing
per means 'a' or 'an', as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A sceptic says nothing an American produces actually functions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a verb but is a plural noun: OPERA is the plural of opus, a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus means a work; its Latin plural opera means works, used of compositions.

clue.text: Boss I introduced to nude swimming without thinking it through

indicators.note: something introduced to another is put inside it
swimming suggests the letters are moving about in a jumble

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised ornamental knob

explanation.surface: An employer speaks of being presented to a skinny-dipper on impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like an employer but is a raised ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unstudied is spontaneous and unpremeditated, done without forethought.

clue.text: Energetic spinner clever with tail end

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
the heel is the back end, as of a loaf

explanation.surface: A lively cricket bowler is crafty with the end of the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket bowler of spin; it is a wheel storing energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flywheel is a heavy rotating wheel that stores kinetic energy in a machine.

clue.text: Meanwhile, Johnson keeps trotting out the same phrases over and over

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Boris Johnson was Prime Minister, PM

parts.words: trotting out the same phrases over and over
parts.note: learning or reciting by rote is mechanical repetition

explanation.surface: A jibe at Boris Johnson, the former Prime Minister, for repeating the same slogans endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem, short for Latin pro tempore, means for the time being, in the meantime.
